cf.title: BUG #19705: One NaN box makes BRIN and GiST box indexes omit unrelated rows

input.subject: BUG #19705: One NaN box makes a BRIN box_inclusion_ops index omit unrelated rows

verdict_reasoning: The bug is a reported wrong-results case with reproductions, and no objection survived at levels 1a or 1b. The one surviving objection, maintenance-fit-2, is a fixable design choice: master would carry box_mergeable while back branches carry the self-containment check. The author already offers to use one check everywhere, so a committer who knows BRIN can settle it.

brief.title: Fix BRIN and GiST box indexes losing rows next to a NaN box
brief.problem: One box value with a NaN coordinate puts NaN into a BRIN range summary or a GiST union key, and no box operator is true against a NaN bound. Index scans then skip the whole page range or subtree, so queries silently return fewer rows than a seq scan. GiST KNN searches with a NaN in a key or query point also fail with "inconsistent point values".
brief.proposed_design: On master, BRIN box_inclusion_ops gets a box_mergeable support function so a range holding a NaN is marked unmergeable and always scanned. Back branches instead scan any range whose union does not contain itself, with no catalog change. GiST unions replace NaN with infinity, old NaN internal keys match every search with KNN distance 0, and leaf ~=, polygon, circle and KNN checks handle NaN.
user_visible_surface: New pg_amproc row for box_inclusion_ops (support function 12, box_mergeable) on master, with a catversion bump.
New GiST box index keys store Infinity where NaN used to appear, visible through gist_page_items.
v1 only: bound_box() returns an infinite bound for a NaN coordinate; later versions leave bound_box() unchanged.
Index scans return rows they omitted before; a count in create_index.out changes from 4 to 5.
author_claims: Old BRIN and GiST indexes return correct results after the fix without REINDEX, checked after pg_upgrade and a minor upgrade.
A differential check of 6769 seq scan versus index comparisons per build drops to zero mismatches, except point <@ polygon with a NaN vertex.
GiST patches 0002 to 0004 and the catalog-free BRIN fix back-patch to 14 with small rebases.
The self-containment check could replace box_mergeable on master to avoid a catversion bump.
The remaining polygon case is a heap bug in point_inside() and belongs in a separate master-only patch.
brief.thread_state: Kirill Reshke, Andrey Borodin and Manu reviewed and tested through v6, and the author asked Tomas and Heikki to commit. John Naylor pointed to a Tom Lane message suggesting a different approach; the author replied that banning NaN cannot be back-patched, and no committer has answered.
unclear: The material does not show what Tom Lane's linked message proposes, beyond the author's summary that it bans NaN.
No committer has chosen between box_mergeable and the self-containment check for master.
The material gives no performance cost of the extra NaN checks in GiST search and KNN paths.
SP-GiST box_ops and poly_ops mismatches are left unfixed, with no plan stated.
The material does not say whether the rebases for 14 to 16 exist yet.

prior_attempts.title: Fix behavior of geo_ops when NaN is involved
prior_attempts.quote: Rather than code changes, what this patch needs is more community interest.
prior_attempts.reason: Tom Lane committed parts of the work in November 2020. The rest was rebased, and a reviewer was asked for comments in March 2021, but no reviewer answered that request or the expanded patch set posted in December 2021. Jacob Champion returned the entry in August 2022 for lack of reviewer interest, and said this was not a rejection.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P1 changed what geo_ops operators return for NaN. This proposal leaves the operators alone and fixes BRIN and GiST so index scans match the heap. It also has three reviewers who tested it, which P1 lacked.

objections.title: Two different BRIN fixes for master and back branches
objections.failure_scenario: A committer later back-patches a fix in brin_inclusion_consistent() or brin_inclusion_add_value(). Master has the box_mergeable path and the back branches have the self-containment check, so the patch conflicts. A hand-merged version on 14 to 18 then gets no testing against the master code.
objections.argument: Message #7 places box_mergeable plus a consistent-side guard on master, and a separate self-containment check on 14 to 18. Messages #7, #14 and #16 say the self-containment check also works on master and needs no catversion bump. Master would then keep a pg_amproc row it does not need for the old-summary case. If master later bans NaN as message #15 suggests, the extra support function stays forever.
objections.author_must_show: What does box_mergeable give on master that the catalog-free self-containment check does not, enough to justify carrying two BRIN fixes?

critic.reasoning: Messages #7, #14 and #16 say the self-containment check works on master with no catalog change, and no message says what box_mergeable adds beyond matching the inet practice. The author offers to switch, so this is a choice for the committer; the NaN ban part is unsupported.

refuted.title: Master BRIN fix adds a catalog row a planned NaN ban may make unneeded
refuted.failure_scenario: A committer pushes 0001 to master, adding box_mergeable as pg_amproc support function 12 with a catversion bump. Master later rejects NaN box input, following the approach John Naylor pointed to. The support function and catalog row then remain, while back branches keep a second, different BRIN fix for the same bug.
refuted.argument: Message #15 points to an earlier message as a different perspective. Message #16 summarizes it as banning NaN, and the material does not show that message itself. Message #16 says on-disk NaN boxes survive pg_upgrade, so master needs some index fix. That argues for the catalog-free self-containment check, which messages #7, #14 and #16 already offer for master, more than for a new support function.
refuted.author_must_show: What does box_mergeable on master give that the catalog-free self-containment check does not, if NaN input may later be banned on master?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-2. This version also rests on a NaN ban that the material shows only through the author's one-line summary in message #16.

refuted.title: Master adds a catalog support function where a catalog-free check exists
refuted.failure_scenario: Master ships box_mergeable as pg_amproc support function 12 and back branches ship the self-containment check, so BRIN box scans run different code by branch. If master later rejects NaN input, as the linked Tom Lane message suggests, the catalog row stays only for old data and cannot be removed easily.
refuted.argument: Message #7 and message #14 say the self-containment check works on master and needs no catversion bump. Message #16 offers it as the smaller option, but no committer has chosen. Message #15 points to another direction for master, banning NaN, and the proposal does not say how a permanent pg_amproc row fits that direction. One code path in all branches is easier to defend, and easier to back-patch fixes into.
refuted.author_must_show: What does box_mergeable do on master that the self-containment check does not, given that master may later forbid NaN boxes?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-2, which states the same choice between box_mergeable and the self-containment check without relying on the unseen linked message.

refuted.title: Back-patched 0003 makes index scans match a heap answer called wrong
refuted.failure_scenario: After a minor upgrade on 14 to 18, a GiST point <@ polygon query starts returning (NaN,NaN) as inside the polygon, as the create_index.out count change from 4 to 5 shows. A later master-only point_inside() fix removes that row again, so the answer changes twice and differs between branches for the same query.
refuted.argument: Message #9 and message #13 say point_inside() puts (NaN,NaN) inside every polygon and call that a heap bug for a separate master-only patch. 0003 is planned for back branches, so it changes what back-branch index scans return to match that behaviour. Making index and seq scans agree is a fair goal, but the proposal does not weigh this against the planned master change.
refuted.author_must_show: Should 0003 be back-patched before the point_inside() behaviour on master is settled, and which answer should back branches give for a NaN point?

critic.reasoning: Back branches today return 4 or 5 rows for the same query depending on the plan, and 0003 removes that difference. The point_inside() change is planned for master only, so back-branch answers change once, and a behavior change in a new major version is normal.

refuted.title: NaN handling spread across GiST call sites with no single rule
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a GiST strategy or distance case for box, polygon or circle without a NaN check. Index scans then drop rows again or fail with "inconsistent point values". Nothing fails at build or regression time, so users find out from wrong query results.
refuted.argument: v6 fixes NaN in GiST unions, the ~= leaf check, polygon and circle consistent cases, and KNN distances, one case at a time as tests found them (messages #4, #8, #10, #11). SP-GiST box_ops and poly_ops mismatches stay unfixed with no stated plan (message #12). Geometric NaN semantics already lack a shared rule, and earlier attempts to settle them stalled for want of reviewers [P1]. No committer who knows GiST or the geometric code has engaged yet.
refuted.author_must_show: What one rule for NaN in box keys does the set follow, and where is it enforced so that a future GiST strategy or SP-GiST change cannot miss it?

precedents.title: Fix behavior of geo_ops when NaN is involved

critic.reasoning: A future GiST strategy without a NaN check is a risk that exists today without the patch, and the set adds none. The set does state its rule in messages #6, #7 and #11, and P1 was returned for lack of reviewers, so it does not support the objection.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: New GiST box keys store Infinity where NaN appeared, and old NaN summaries and keys must still be read correctly after pg_upgrade.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: Master adds a pg_amproc row for box_inclusion_ops (support function 12, box_mergeable) with a catversion bump.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The GiST patches and a catalog-free BRIN fix are planned for back-patch to 14, with a different BRIN fix on master.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Two BRIN fixes by branch, plus NaN checks in several GiST consistent, union and KNN code paths.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: Extra NaN checks run in GiST search and KNN distance paths, and the thread gives no measurement.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: What does box_mergeable give on master that the catalog-free self-containment check does not, enough to justify two different BRIN fixes?
What is the measured cost of the added NaN checks in GiST search and KNN paths for box indexes that hold no NaN?
Do the rebased patches for 14 to 16 exist, and do they pass the same differential check of seq scan against index scan?
What is the plan for the SP-GiST box_ops and poly_ops mismatches that this set leaves unfixed?
What does the Tom Lane message that John Naylor linked propose for master, and how does this set fit with it?

committability.owner_note: Needs a committer who knows the BRIN inclusion framework and the GiST geometric opclasses. The author asked Tomas and Heikki to commit, and neither has answered in the visible thread.
committability.liability: A back-patch to 14 that changes index scan results and GiST key contents, plus on master a permanent pg_amproc row. The owner also signs that old NaN summaries and keys stay correct without REINDEX.
committability.author_follow_up: Good sign: the authors posted six versions in response to review and offer to switch the master BRIN fix to the self-containment check.

priority.reason: Few tables hold NaN boxes, but affected users get silently wrong results, and three reviewers have tested the set. It waits on a committer to choose the master BRIN fix; review cost is estimated because no code was read.

provisional_note: Without the code, the claims that old NaN summaries and internal keys are handled without REINDEX, and that the self-containment check catches every poisoned range, could not be checked. Only the first 3 of 16 messages were read directly.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix behavior of geo_ops when NaN is involved
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes the geometric functions in geo_ops.c handle NaN consistently: boolean operators no longer return true for NaN inputs, and distance functions return NaN. A later version adds tri-state geometric comparisons that return NULL when NaN is involved, with GiST treating NULL as false.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane committed parts of the work in November 2020. The rest was rebased, and a reviewer was asked for comments in March 2021, but no reviewer answered that request or the expanded patch set posted in December 2021. Jacob Champion returned the entry in August 2022 for lack of reviewer interest, and said this was not a rejection.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Rather than code changes, what this patch needs is more community interest.

precedents_retrieved.title: support for box type in SP-GiST index
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set adds an SP-GiST operator class for the box type that treats a 2D box as a point in 4D space and indexes it with a quad-tree analogue (q4d) splitting each node into 16 regions. It also adds a traversalValue field to SP-GiST so inner_consistent can carry computed bounds to child nodes, and switches range_spgist.c from reconstructValue to it.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers asked for performance numbers, a fuller explanation of the patch's purpose, and a rebase, and the patch was set to Waiting on Author. The author did not reply, so it was closed after about three months without a response.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I closed this patch as "returned with feedback" because the author
didn't reply in three months.

precedents_retrieved.title: Floating point comparison inconsistencies of the geometric types
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patches remove the EPSILON-based fuzzy comparison macros (FPeq, FPlt, and others) from most geometric operators and use exact floating point comparison, with fuzzy comparison kept only for some lseg operators. They also rewrite some line operators to avoid division and add overflow, underflow and NaN checks, to allow default btree and hash operator classes and more index support later.
precedents_retrieved.objection: There was no agreement to remove the tolerance. Kyotaro HORIGUCHI argued that geometric types need a tolerance for floating point error, and Robert Haas rejected the GUC that came out of that discussion because indexes built under one setting could be invalid under another. Robert Haas noted that only the author clearly favoured removal and that nothing could be committed without agreement. The thread then went idle, the patches no longer applied, and David Steele returned the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Those problems boil down to "let's get rid of the tolerance
completely", and there's no consensus on that being a good thing to
do.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Change default value of default_toast_compression to "lz4""
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Change default value of default_toast_compression to "lz4""
Reverted commit(s): Change default value of default_toast_compression to "lz4", when available
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 7c1849311e49, due to the fact that more than 60% of
the buildfarm members do not have lz4 installed.  As we are in the last
commit fest of the development cycle, and that it could take a couple
of weeks to stabilize things, this change is reverted for now.

This commit will be reworked in a lighter version, as
default_toast_compression's default can be changed to "lz4" without the
switch from --with-lz4 to --without-lz4.  This approach will keep the
buildfarm at bay, and still allow builds to take advantage of LZ4 in
TOAST by default, as long as the code is compiled with LZ4 support.

A harder requirement based on LZ4 should be achievable at some point,
but it is going to require some work from the buildfarm owners first.
Perhaps this part could be revisited at the beginning of the next
development cycle.

precedents_retrieved.title: When deleting the plpgsql function, release the CachedPlan of the function
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Matthias van de Meent, Tom Lane
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch frees the CachedPlan contexts of a PL/pgSQL function or procedure when DROP FUNCTION or DROP PROCEDURE runs, so they no longer stay in CacheMemoryContext until the session ends. The author showed with pg_get_backend_memory_contexts() that a dropped and recreated procedure leaves two sets of CachedPlan contexts.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch frees cached plans only in the backend that runs the DROP, because other sessions do not execute RemoveFunctionById and keep their plans. Tom Lane suggested that PL/pgSQL, or funccache.c so SQL functions also benefit, install a shared-cache-invalidation callback on pg_proc that marks function trees as deletable. The author agreed, linked a new thread, and withdrew this entry. Vladlen Popolitov also asked why the plans should be freed at all.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: It doesn't, which is (one reason) why it's just a crude hack.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix inconsistency in reporting checkpointer stats
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes a mismatch between the checkpoint log message and the checkpointer statistics view: the log counts SLRU page writes in SlruInternalWritePage() as written buffers, but the view counts only BufferSync() writes. Later versions count SLRU writes in a separate slru_written column in pg_stat_checkpointer and list them separately in the log message.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why the entry closed as Returned with feedback, because Fujii Masao pushed the final version on 2024-10-02. Earlier, in January 2024, Michael Paquier returned an older entry because the patch no longer applied and columns had moved from pg_stat_bgwriter to pg_stat_checkpointer.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Some of the columns of pg_stat_bgwriter have
been moved to a different view, aka pg_stat_checkpointer.

precedents_retrieved.title: PGDOCS - inconsistent linkends to "monitoring" views
precedents_retrieved.summary: Rename a few documentation IDs and their linkends in the monitoring chapter (pg_stat_recovery_prefetch, pg_stat_subscription, pg_stat_subscription_stats) to add the "-view" suffix. This would make them match the naming used by all the other statistics views.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier asked whether renaming internal link references was worth it, since it could cause extra backpatching conflicts. John Naylor agreed the existing links were not wrong and the change was not visible to readers. No one came out in favor of the patch, so it was rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
In any case, no one has come out in favor of the patch, so it seems
like it should be rejected unless that changes.

precedents_retrieved.title: Inconsistency in owner assignment between INDEX and STATISTICS
precedents_retrieved.summary: The proposal makes CREATE STATISTICS record the table owner as the owner of the statistics object, as CREATE INDEX does, in place of the user who runs the command. The patch sets stxowner from the relation's relowner in CreateStatistics() and keeps the permission check on the current user.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amit Khandekar pointed out that the documentation states statistics ownership is independent of the underlying table, so the creator owning the object is intended. He also showed that the reproduction was wrong: the statistics object was created in the default schema, and dropping it there gives the expected "must be owner" error. The author agreed with both points and withdrew the proposal.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think, since there is no permanent association of ownership between
the table and the statistics, it makes sense for the user who is
running the create command to own the statistics, regardless of who
the user is, provided that the user has privileges.

precedents_retrieved.title: elog/ereport VS misleading backtrace_function function address
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds one dummy instruction to the ereport_domain macro, between errfinish() and pg_unreachable() for elevel >= ERROR, so that backtrace_functions reports an address inside the right function. Without it, in optimized builds without --enable-debug, the return address of the .cold error branch falls into the next function's cold section, and addr2line names the wrong function.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers found no principled explanation of why the extra instruction fixes the address, so the fix may stop working with another compiler, platform or compiler version. Robert Haas also objected on principle to adding junk code to get good backtraces. He and Alvaro Herrera pointed to installing debug symbols as the right fix.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Unless we really understand
why the results are better with that nop instruction added, we can't
possibly have any confidence that this is anything other than random
good fortune, which isn't a sufficiently good reason to make a change.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent records a rejection reason that applies to this bug fix. P4 died over removing the epsilon tolerance, and this proposal keeps the tolerance. P5 records no reason.
The bug fix itself fits existing practice. It adds no new syntax and no GUC, and dump behaviour does not change. Old indexes are reported correct after pg_upgrade and minor upgrade.

No objections from the on-disk and replication angle. The back-branch fixes change no on-disk format, WAL record or catalog, and the patched scan code accepts summaries and NaN internal keys written by old binaries, so pg_upgrade, minor upgrade, a minor downgrade and mixed-minor standbys keep returning correct results. Infinity keys are already handled by old binaries, the master pg_amproc row reaches pg_upgraded indexes through the new catalog, and no ABI-visible struct or hook changes.

The proposal adds no privilege, role, function exposure or new information path; it fixes index scans that return fewer rows than a seq scan. A user with INSERT can force wider scans with a NaN box, but an infinite box already does the same, so no new denial-of-service path follows.
This is a data-correctness bug fix, and its core goal is sound. Both objections ask for a smaller, more uniform shape. Neither argues against fixing the bug.

No existing feature or extension stops BRIN and GiST box indexes from returning fewer rows than a seq scan, so this angle finds nothing to object to. A CHECK constraint can keep new NaN boxes out, but it does not repair existing indexes or GiST KNN errors. The master BRIN fix extends the existing INCLUSION_UNMERGEABLE support-function mechanism, which inet already uses, instead of adding a second one.

This is a wrong-results bug with a field report (message #1, Postgres 18.6) and reproductions by four people. Index scans silently drop rows that hold no NaN, so the problem is real and needs no further demand evidence. Whether box_mergeable is needed on master, or the self-containment check is enough, is a design question for other angles.
